notes.title: Difficulty settings & Control mapping update
notes.notes:
[h1]Greetings, pilots![/h1]

[h2]Price drop[/h2]

First things first: The price for Gravity Ace has dropped significantly! If you were waiting for the price to come down then your prayers have been answered. Go get it now.

[h2]Difficulty settings[/h2]

Gravity Ace now has three difficulty settings that affect fuel consumption. At the easiest level, fuel is consumed much slower. And at the hardest level fuel is consumed faster. If you want the most challenging experience where fuel management is a very important part of the game then you want Hard diffculty. If you just want to shoot things and not worry about fuel so much, choose Easy.

[h2]Auto targeting[/h2]

Along with the new difficulty settings you can also choose to use a targeting computer that will automagically select the closest target for destruction. You still control when you shoot but you don't need to aim anymore. Be careful and shoot wisely because one of the targets is the reactor core if you are not carrying it. You can now play Gravity Ace without using the right stick or mouse. This also makes the Classic mode controls (rotate and thrust) easier to manage. Hopefully this helps improve accessibility and lets you enjoy more explosions.

[h2]Control remapping[/h2]

Controller mapping is in! You can change keymaps and controller buttons within the game from the Options menu. It does what you'd expect. Enjoy!

notes.title: Modern twin-stick cave-flyer 'Gravity Ace' is out now and it's great
notes.notes:
Remember the days when games were a lot simpler, and you had various attempts at cave-flying? Well, I do and the new release Gravity Ace brings back some fun memories while making a modern spin.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2022/05/modern-twin-stick-cave-flyer-gravity-ace-is-out-now-and-its-great

notes.title: Gravity Ace available May 26!
notes.notes:
Hey folks! It's a been a long time coming but [b]Gravity Ace is leaving early access today![/b] Thank you to everybody who has stuck around for the ride!

Early Access took longer than expected (let's blame Covid) but I think it's worth the wait. Gravity Ace now includes [b]50 levels of content in 2 campaigns, boss fights, many new enemies to fight, new mechanics like gravity rivers, an original soundtrack, and a built-in level editor[/b] that lets you share your creations with others. In fact, in case you didn't know, all of the levels in Gravity Ace were made with Gravity Ace!

We're celebrating reaching this destination with a [b]significant launch discount.[/b] Try the demo, play the game, tell your friends, share your levels!

And this isn't the end of the road. I intend to continue working on the game. Specifically, supporting players with post-launch fixes, new mechanics, new enemies, and new levels. I have a fun idea for including a set of levels made by the community! [b]The future is bright![/b]

[b]Thanks again for your support and help along the way! Enjoy the game![/b]

notes.title: Small fixes prior to release!
notes.notes: Hey, folks! Release day is nearly upon us and of course I'm making some last minute fixes. The most notable in this release is that the hitbox for the player was adjusted so that it's smaller. There was a bug making it a wee bit bigger than it should have been which, in some situations, felt Bad(tm). But it's all fixed, enjoy pilots!

notes.title: Gravity Ace is leaving Early Access on May 26th!
notes.notes:
It's been a long road, a little too long if I'm being totally honest with myself, but it's worth the wait. Over the past 17 months I've put in a ton of polish, lots of new enemies and levels, and improved the level editor significantly. I think you're going to have a lot of fun!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34418867/1844e8dd66dbaa4c53de720fa2027d4f6ca6dd25.png[/img]

The level editor has a ton of fun new features like new event triggers, more dialog options, new enemies and bosses, new terrain, secret walls, and a lot more. All 50 levels that will ship with the full game were made with the level editor that comes with it. And you can easily export levels to share with your friends or the community. I can't wait to see what you can make!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34418867/445b766bb671dc714e42f2fa0022a92624988c7c.png[/img]

The new campaign has 25 levels, just like the first, with all new puzzles and challenges in store. And there are built-in options specifically for speedrunning and streaming that I think you're going to enjoy.

It's been a [i]long[/i] road but May 26th is [i]not[/i] the [i]end[/i] of the road. I'm planning more features post-launch including new toys for the level editor, new game modes, and more campaign content.

Thank you for coming along on this journey with me. It's truly been a wonderful experience! See you out there, Pilots!

notes.title: Gravity Ace is an excellent take on classic twin-stick cave-flying and it feels awesome
notes.notes:
Cave-flying is a genre that was big a very long time ago, now though not so much but Gravity Ace from John Watson entered Early Access recently and it's absolutely brilliant.

Read the full article here: https://www.gamingonlinux.com/2020/10/gravity-ace-is-an-excellent-take-on-classic-twin-stick-cave-flying-and-it-feels-awesome

notes.title: Early Access October 22!
notes.notes:
Well, folks, the time is almost upon us. Gravity Ace is finally in a state where I can release it into the wild. [b]Gravity Ace will launch in Early Access October 22.[/b] What does that mean exactly?

The current game is fully playable with a 24 mission main campaign, fully integrated level editor, highly polished art and sound, and a great soundtrack. But it isn't done yet! I want Gravity Ace to be a satisfying and rewarding experience for new players and fans of the amazing classic arcade games it's based on. Community feedback has been [i]vital[/i] during the development process. I'm looking forward to expanding the community through Early Access and using your feedback to shape and balance Gravity Ace so that it's as fun and polished as it can possibly be.

I have big plans for Early Access! I want to add new enemies, bosses, more levels and campaigns, fix bugs (of course), and add a local multiplayer mode for player-vs-player battles. A major component of Gravity Ace is the built-in level editor. The editor is very robust and allows anyone to make levels just like the ones included with the game. I plan to enhance that by allowing players to share levels and entire campaigns with one another through a central hub. The plan is that you'll be able to play other players' shared campaigns which will add a continuous stream of new content for you to enjoy.

It's going to take another 6-12 months to finish all of that work. [b]I need your help![/b] Please tell everyone you know about Gravity Ace! Help me spread the word and ask people to add it to their wishlist! The more of us there are, the better the game, and the more fun it'll be. It's been great fun so far and I'm looking forward to what's ahead.

[i]From the bottom of my heart, thank you![/i]
